_about: Hand-authored FR-9 frame-check cases with expected verdicts in BOTH directions (EVALS M5b). Each case starts from a real buy decision taken from the scenario-A replay, injects the named user-supplied strings, optionally mutates the generated text (simulating a tampered template or renderer) or the decision, and then runs the engine's own render + frame check. 'block' means the check must reject; 'render' means it must accept. A wrongly blocked must-render case is a compliance failure, not caution: real Grailed titles say 'guaranteed authentic'.

cases.why: The collectibles-not-advice footer must render verbatim; softening it is the classic way a disclaimer stops disclaiming.

mutate.with: not investment advice, though the model is rarely wrong.

cases.why: An advice with no footer at all cannot be persisted (store CHECK frame_checked = 1).
Section omission: dropping the fee/illiquidity note removes both a required section and the quoted friction.
Section omission: advice without its drivers is an unfalsifiable assertion.
A forbidden phrase emitted by the renderer itself (not quoted user text) must block.

mutate.text: At this level the piece is a sure thing.

cases.why: Certainty language in a generated headline is exactly what the lexicon exists to stop.
theta == fee_assumption_pct, so an actionable advice quoting a move smaller than its own friction contradicts itself on the page (SCOPE D-12).
The fee note must render the configured fee_assumption_pct; a rewritten number makes the safeguard cosmetic.
A real marketplace label — 'guaranteed authentic' — is user text in quotes and must not block the advice (over-blocking is the M5b failure).
An event note the user pasted from a seller carries a forbidden phrase in quoted context.

cases.why: A listing title quoted into the event note ('easy money') is user-supplied text, not a product claim.

cases.why: A label carrying a typographic closing quote must not be able to smuggle text out of the quoted span; the renderer strips it, so the advice still renders and the lexicon still cannot be evaded.
Label and event note both carry forbidden phrases in quoted context; the advice must still render.
